To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) NMR spectroscopy is a sensitive and powerful technique for the study of the substrate specificity of enzymes, (2) the "polar gating" theory is a useful concept for the interpretation of NMR data and (3) NMR spectroscopical methods are a powerful tool in the elucidation of the dynamics of enzymatic reactions with carbohydrates.
the substrate specificity of oligosaccha- ride degrading enzymes can be explained by the polar gate theory and by the ground state minimum energy conformations in the solution of the oligosacharides.

the specificity and the binding of oligosaccha- rides to enzymes can be understood by a combination of chemical modifications of the oligosach— aride, NMR studies of the oligosaccaride in solution and X—ray data from the enzyme—oligosacharide complexes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the structure and conformation of carbohydrates, the study of their interaction with enzymes, and the application of high field NMR to the analysis of dynamic enzymatic processes.
the elucidation of the molecular basis of enzyme—substrate interaction in carbohydrate hydrolysis.
the structure— function relationships of oligosaccha- rides, and the results obtained so far are important for the understanding of the enzymatic degradation of polysaccharides.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the structure of oligosaccha- rides in solution can be predicted by the use of high field NMR spec— troscopy and that the structure of these compounds bound to enzymes can be determined by a combined use of high field and conventional X— ray diffraction techniques.

the substrate specificity of the enzymes used in the hydrolysis of starch and cellulose can be understood in terms of the structure of the oligosacharides, the conformations of the carbohydrate substrat— es in solution and the binding of the substrates to the enzymes in the active site.

the structure of the carbohydrate is of crucial importance for the binding and subsequent reaction with enzymes, and that high field NMR is a powerful and sensitive tool for the determination of these structures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NMR spectroscopy is a very useful technique in the elucidation of structure—function relationships in oligo— saccharide—enzyme interactions.
the substrate specificities of enzymes involved in the degradation of starch and cellulose can be rationalized in terms of the structure of the oligosacharide substrates.
NMR spectroscopy has become a powerful tool for the study of carbohydrate-protein interactions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
NMR spectroscopy is an indispensable tool in the characterization of oligosaccha- ride substrates and in the study of enzymatic reactions.

high field NMR is an extremely powerful and versatile tool to study the structure and dynamics of carbohydrates in solution, and that it can be combined with other methods such as X—ray crystallography to give a complete picture of the interactions between carbohydrates and proteins.
the combination of NMR spectroscopy and computational chemistry can be used to understand the structure and function of carbohydrates and their interactions with proteins.
